[operator-attested] Final live-run attestation for the scheduling-affecting criterion.

Ran the remediation twice. Cumulative: 12 edges repaired (all 9 ancestor-blocking, plus 3 mis-escalated), 8 residual.

Residual verification — for each of the 8 remaining findings I resolved the BLOCKED side (source for depends_on, target for blocks) and read its status:
- 03a9-e6d1-4acc-435d (closed)
- 2aa6-726a-ea56-4d6c (closed)
- 38be-a778-43f5-4a4e (closed)
- 8d39-85d7-8f34-45e6 (closed)
- 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d (closed)
- 8784-c2d7-c395-4478 (closed)  [blocks relation, so the target is the blocked side]
- e3bd-8cd2-35f1-406b (closed)
- ea39-c2d1-e26a-4ee6 (closed)

All 8 closed => 0 of 8 can appear in ready or next-batch => 0 scheduling-affecting findings. Criterion met.

Each is blocked from repair by add_dependency refusing a link whose source is closed (src/rebar/graph/_links.py:254), which is correct behaviour.

DRIFT FINDING — the store does not stay clean on its own. Between the two runs the scan went 8 -> 10: two NEW mis-escalated edges appeared, both from 2682-b015-4fe5-4066, and unlike the residuals BOTH had open blocked sides, so they were genuinely distorting scheduling. Repaired in 13.7s and 3.1s. The likely mechanism is re-parenting, which silently invalidates a previously-correct edge without touching the link itself. This makes link-audit an ongoing check rather than a one-shot cleanup; its exit-1-while-outstanding contract already suits a periodic CI run. Recorded here as a follow-up, not fixed under this ticket.
